changes: Adjusted operating margin doubled to 10% (5% in 2Q, 1% in 1Q); FY26 adjusted operating income guide raised 26% at the midpoint, implying about 16.5% in 4Q at the midpoint (15-18% across the range).
Funding plan reframed: no new parent unsecured debt at current yields through 2027, under $5bn of parent-level capital needed, next delayed-draw loan talked at about 7-7.5%.
About $9bn of customer prepayments and deposits due in the next three months; prepayments on about 70% of this year's deals.
Backlog about $132.5bn (+27% QoQ); contracted power above 4.6 GW (+over 900 MW); active power above 1.7 GW (+over 200 MW).
Total debt $46.9bn, up $11.8bn QoQ; 4Q interest guided to $1.05-1.15bn; capex of $14.5bn (management basis) ran above the top of the guide.
checks: Post-call. Results from the 3Q26 release (SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1, 10 November) and the 2Q26 and 3Q25 releases; call content from four transcripts (Investing.com, Motley Fool via AOL, Equibles, TradingKey) that agree on six analysts. 10-Q not yet filed, so 3Q customer concentration, maturities and ATM usage are missing. Derived figures (growth, margins, total and net debt, funding gap, EBITDA less interest, coverage, implied 4Q = FY guide less 9M) recomputed in Python. A fresh subagent checked about 93 items against the sources: about 85 confirmed; fixed: bond yields (2032s above 16%, not 15-16%), 'half junk-bond yields' attributed to The Next Web not Bloomberg, implied 4Q margin restated as ~16.5% at midpoints (15-18% range). Unverifiable from today's sources and carried from the 5 November preview: prior 3Q guides ($3.45-3.6bn revenue, $860-940mn interest), prior FY adjusted operating income guide ($0.96-1.15bn; consistent with the release's +26% at midpoint), Goldman's +100-200bp view. Microsoft supplier-cut report is single source (Dataconomy). Share price: $48.73 close 10 November; about $56 (+16%) early 11 November per 24/7 Wall St; no bond or CDS quote dated 10-11 November found. EPS consensus conflicting across sources and not used.
consensus_thesis: Investors own CoreWeave for take-or-pay backlog, tight supply and rising price per MW, and avoid it for leverage, refinancing and customer credit; going in, the stock (about $48) and bonds (2032s above 16%, CDS above 1,100bp) priced a funding problem, not an operating one.
headline: The market's funding-crisis view should soften: a beat-and-raise quarter plus a plan to fund 2027 almost entirely at asset level (under $5bn of parent capital, about $9bn of prepayments in three months) strengthens the thesis, but debt rose $11.8bn in the quarter and credit relief now depends on the next delayed-draw loan pricing near 7-7.5%.
kona: CoreWeave has put a price on tenant credit: its delayed-draw loans run from about 225bp over SOFR for investment-grade customers to 550bp for AI labs, and prepayments on about 70% of deals are its cheapest capital. For Kona: price contracts to win prepayment, and prefer investment-grade or large-enterprise tenants over labs if it ever finances GPUs; short-dated capacity at about $40mn per MW against $20-25mn long-dated shows the premium for flexibility. Reopened secured lending helps a Kona tenant fund GPUs, but power-only or hosting still keeps Kona out of the spread.
monitor: Pricing and rating of the next delayed-draw loan (talked at 7-7.5%, 'high investment grade' expected).
4Q adjusted operating margin against the implied ~16.5%, and active power above 1.85 GW at year-end.
10-Q: top-customer concentration, debt maturities, ATM usage and the basis of the $14.5bn capex figure.

sections.body: More: funding self-sufficiency (prepayments, asset-level loans, a 'high investment grade' rating hoped for on the next loan); EBITDA less interest as a 2027 target; re-contracting of paid-off GPUs (about 130k roll off in 2027, about 170k in 2028) as roughly $4bn of 2027 ARR outside backlog; enterprise and financial-services customers (10% of backlog). Less or dropped: unsecured bonds as a funding source; any 2026 revenue-per-quarter guide (only FY and 4Q interest given); a total funding-gap number. KPIs gaining weight: EBITDA less interest, prepayments, weighted cost of debt. Losing weight: headline backlog growth on its own. → The narrative moved from growth to funding discipline. That is what the market wanted to hear; it now has to show up in loan pricing and 4Q interest.

sections.body: $mn. Funding gap = cash capex less operating cash flow. Net debt = recourse plus non-recourse debt less cash and restricted cash (our sums; excludes $18.7bn of operating leases). Shares = weighted average. Funding in the quarter: $2.6bn DDTL 5.5 at SOFR+550, ~5 years, Ba2/BB+, on contracts averaging ~3 years (August); ~$4.2bn of 2.875% converts due 2033 incl. option (September); ATM for up to 35mn shares (September). What the next dollar costs: secured, contract-backed loans at about 7-7.5% (management; The Next Web puts it at about half junk-bond yields); unsecured 2032s above 16% before results, now avoided. Maturities in 24 months: current debt $10.6bn (recourse $9.2bn, non-recourse $1.4bn) at 30 September. → Do new contracts earn more than their funding cost? Long-dated deals at $20-25mn per MW with 1-2 year payback against 7-8% debt: yes, if lenders keep accepting tenor longer than contracts.
sections.title: Capital and funding

sections.body: Signals: (1) next DDTL size, yield and rating; (2) 4Q adjusted operating margin vs implied ~16.5%; (3) active power at year-end vs 1.85 GW; (4) prepayments collected vs ~$9bn; (5) 10-Q top-customer shares. Risks building: interest rising faster than EBITDA in 4Q; GPU roll-offs repriced lower; Microsoft reducing neocloud suppliers. Confirmation: next loan prices at or below 7.5% with an investment-grade rating; 4Q margin in mid-teens; bonds rally toward 10-12%. Conviction tripwires: a new parent unsecured or discounted equity raise; a delivery slip below 1.85 GW; a large customer reducing commitments.
